column2: When Event Should Fire
column5: Associated Parameters
column6:
Dev Requirements (DL Specs)
//*When a parameter has no value, set it to undefined. Do not send null, an empty string, or text like "n/a", since GA4 stores those as real values. Setting undefined (instead of leaving the key out) also clears any value GTM is still holding from an earlier push.

column2: This event will fire on page load of all pages and capture key page information.
column5:
page_url (full URL of the page, e.g. "https://gab-rodier.github.io/portfolio/work-samples/", "https://gab-rodier.github.io/portfolio/")
page_title (title of the page, e.g. "Contact", "Homepage", "Work Samples", "Skills + Tools")
query_parameter (query string of the page URL if applicable)
page_type (type of page on the site, e.g. "home", "skills + tools", "contact", "work samples")
page_section_path (section of page if applicable, e.g. "#analytics", "#ai", "#operations", "#leadership", "#about")
page_section_title (title of section of page if applicable, e.g. "analytics", "ai", "operations", "leadership", "about")
internal_traffic (set as "true" when a page has "?internal=1" or "&internal=1" in the URL and have this persist through the DL indefinitely with value remembered on the browser until there's a visit with ?internal=0, set as "false" otherwise)

column2: This event will fire on section load of all sections on the homepage (e.g. '#analytics' / '#ai' / '#operations' / '#leadership' / '#about', even when a user is just scrolling there and not clicking to there from a nav link) and capture key page information.
column5:
page_url (full URL of the page, e.g. "https://gab-rodier.github.io/portfolio/")
page_title (title of the page, e.g. "Homepage")
query_parameter (query string of the page URL if applicable)
page_type (type of page on the site, e.g. "home")
page_section_path (section of page, e.g. "#analytics", "#ai", "#operations", "#leadership", "#about")
page_section_title (title of section of page, e.g. "analytics", "ai", "operations", "leadership", "about")

column2: This event will fire the first time a user reaches 25%, 50%, 75%, 90% and 100% scrolled on any page.
column5: page_percentage (scroll depth reached, e.g. "25", "50", "75", "90", "100")

column2: This event will fire each time a user clicks a link that leads away from the current domain.
column5:
click_text (text of the clicked element, e.g. "Connect on LinkedIn")
click_url (destination URL, e.g. "www.linkedin.com/in/gabrodier")
click_domain (destination hostname, e.g. "linkedin.com")

column2: This event will fire when a form comes into view. (e.g. when a user clicks Open to pull out the form on the envelope on the Contact page)
column5:
element_name (form name, e.g. "contact form")
element_id (form ID, e.g. "my-form")
click_text (name of the text clicked to bring the form into view, e.g. "Open")

column2: This event will fire when the user successfully submits a form.
column5:
click_text (text of the form submit button, e.g. "Send Note")
element_name (form name, e.g. "contact form")
element_id (form ID, e.g. "my-form")
form_selection (selected dropdown reason when applicable, e.g. "Reason: Just Saying Hi")

column2: This event will fire when a user clicks any element of the main navigation.
column5:
click_text (text of the clicked element, e.g. "Get in Touch"; use value "logo icon" for icon clicks)
click_url (destination URL, e.g. "gab-rodier.github.io/portfolio/contact/", "gab-rodier.github.io/portfolio/#about")
element_type (type of element, e.g. "link", "button", "icon")
element_location (name of the nav type, e.g. "static", "hamburger")

column2: This event will fire when a user clicks any element of the footer navigation.
column5:
click_text (text of the clicked element, e.g. "AI", "Email Me"; use value "logo icon" for icon clicks)
click_url (destination URL, use value "gab.rodier address" instead of the mailto URL for Email me clicks)
element_type (type of element, e.g. "link", "button", "icon")
element_location (name of the footer section, e.g. "Get in Touch", "Explore"; use value "logo" for icon clicks)

column2: This event will fire when a user clicks to download a file. (e.g. Resume Downloads)
column5:
file_name (e.g. "Gabrielle-Rodier-Resume")
file_extension (e.g. "PDF")
click_url (e.g. "https://gab-rodier.github.io/portfolio/Gabrielle-Rodier-Resume.pdf")
click_text (e.g. "Resume (PDF)", "Download the PDF")

column2: This event will fire when a user clicks a mailto link.
column5:
click_text (text of the clicked link, e.g. "Email me", "gab.rodier address")
element_location (name of where the link lives, e.g. "footer", "contact page")

column2: This event will fire when a user clicks a 'Copy' link to copy text like my email.
column5:
click_text (text of the clicked link, e.g. "Copy")
element_location (name of where the link lives, e.g. "footer")
element_name (name of what's being copied, e.g. "gab.rodier address")

column2: This event will fire when a user interacts with the Maturity Framework tool (e.g. selected a dropdown or clicked 'See My Result') or the Scoping tool (e.g. selected a checkbox or selected a wide-span update like 'Clear All' / 'Reset to Sample', or selected a multi-choice button like 'Medium' / 'Yes' / 'Light').
column3:
Selected a dropdown like 'A few basic ones' for 'Strategic measurement' field in the Maturity tool,
Clicked 'See My Result' in the Maturity tool,
Selected a checkbox like 'Discovery + kickoff' for 'Strategy' section in the Scoping tool,
Selected a wide-span update like 'Clear All' / 'Reset to Sample' in the Scoping tool,
Selected a multi-choice button like 'Medium' / 'Yes' / 'Light' in the Scoping tool
column5:
element_type (type of interaction, e.g. "dropdown selection", "submit for result", "checkbox selection", "selections wide-span update", "multi-choice button selection")
element_location (name of the applicable tool, e.g. "Maturity Tool", "Scoping Tool")
element_name (name of aligning interaction item when applicable, e.g. "Data collection", "Strategic measurement", "Reporting", "Data application", "Audience segmentation", "Strategy", "Tracking", "Data Quality", "Reporting", "Consent", "CRO", "Overall business + digital complexity", "Cross-domain journeys", "Ecommerce", "Server-side tagging", "Stakeholder + admin load")
click_text (text of the interaction clicked, e.g. "level 2" //NOTE: use level number of selected dropdown for maturity tool, "See My Result", "Clear All", "Reset to Sample", "checkbox section option 3" //NOTE: use index number within the given section of selected checkbox for scoping tool, "High", "Yes", "Heavy")

column2: This event will fire when a user opens a pop-up modal or tool. (e.g. a Case Study or a Work Sample or the Maturity Framework Tool or the Estimates Tool)
column3:
Clicks on "Read the case" on the Department Turnaround and Growth card in the Operations section mid-page on the homepage,
Clicks on "Open the dashboard" on the Executive Dashboard card on the Work Samples page,
Clicks on "Open The Tool" in the Maturity Tool area of the Analytics section mid-page on the homepage,
Clicks on "Open The Tool" in the Scope Tool area of the Operations section mid-page on the homepage
column5:
click_text (text of the element that opened the modal, e.g. "Read the case", "Open the dashboard", "Open The Tool")
element_name (descriptive name of the modal, e.g. "Department Turnaround and Growth Case Study", "Executive Dashboard Work Sample", "Maturity Framework Tool")
element_type (category of the modal, e.g. "Case Study", "Work Sample", "Tool")

column2: This event will fire when a user closes a pop-up modal or tool. (e.g. a Case Study or a Work Sample or a Tool)
column3:
Clicks to exit the Department Turnaround and Growth popup in the Operations section mid-page on the homepage,
Clicks to exit the Executive Dashboard popup on the Work Samples page,
Clicks to exit the Maturity Tool of the Analytics section mid-page on the homepage,
Clicks to exit the Scope Tool of the Operations section mid-page on the homepage
column5:
element_name (descriptive name of the modal, e.g. "Department Turnaround and Growth Case Study", "Executive Dashboard Work Sample", "Maturity Framework Tool")
element_type (category of the modal, e.g. "Case Study", "Work Sample", "Tool")

column2: This event will fire when a user clicks to exapand any content on the page or popup module. (e.g. tabs, expandable titles, etc)
column3:
Clicking a step like 'Test or Ship' in The Cycle of UX Data section on /portfolio/#analytics, 
Clicking a tab like 'Key Events' in Tracking Plan + Audit Excerpt work sample popup, 
Clicking a tab like 'Content' in Executive Dashboard work sample popup,
Clicking a folder tab like 'Analytics + UX' in the Toolkit Hightlights section on /portfolio/#about,
Clicking a spine like 'Volunteering' in the Off the Clock section on /portfolio/#about.
column5:
click_text (text of the clicked element, e.g. "Test or Ship", "Key Events", "Content", "Analytics + UX", "Volunteering")
element_location (name of the section the expandable content sits in, e.g. "The Cycle of UX Data", "Tracking Plan + Audit Excerpt work sample", "Executive Dashboard work sample", "Toolkit Highlights", "Off the Clock")

column2: This event will fire when a user clicks to make content shift. (e.g. content slider bar or arrow click)
column3:
Slider clicks - arrow or bar - in review feedback quotes section on homepage Leadership section, 
Slider clicks - arrow or bar - in Measurement Strategy Excerpt work sample popup, 
Slider clicks - arrow or bar - in Focused Actionable Analysis work sample popup,
Slider clicks - arrow or bar - in Quarterly Department Review work sample popup
column5:
action (type of slider interaction, e.g. "shift arrow click", "shift bar click")
click_direction (direction of the interaction, use when the slider is shifted, e.g. "forward", "backward")
element_location (name of the slider, e.g. "review feedback quotes" for the Leadership section slider, "Quarterly Department Review work sample")
from_state (slide number that a user is on when clicking to slide elsewhere, e.g. "1-2", "1")
to_state (slide number that a user is clicking to, e.g. "2-3", "2")
total_options (number of total slides that exist in the slider, e.g. "4", "8")

column2: This event will fire when a user opens the main navigation hamburger on small screens like mobile.

This event will fire when a user interacts with any filter. (e.g. clicking a selectable filter option, entering a filter search term) 

//NOTE: for firing on search term filter interactions, wait 2,000ms after typing stops in search bar
column3:
Clicking an Area pill like 'Digital Marketing' or a Level pill like 'Expert' on /portfolio/skills-tools/),
Entering a term like 'platform' in the search bar on the /portfolio/skills-tools/ page,
Selecting a Hostname like 'docs.larkspurlabs.com' or a Date range like 'Last 26 weeks' in the Executive Dashboard work sample popup.
column5:
element_location (name of where filter lives, e.g. "Skills + Tools", "Executive Dashboard work sample")
element_name (filter name, e.g. "Area", "Level", "Search Term", "Hostname, "Date range")
element_type (type of filter element, e.g. "selectable option", "search bar")
filter_selection (selected filter option, e.g. "Digital Marketing, "Expert", "docs.larkspurlabs.com", "Last 26 weeks"; use the entered search term for search filters, use "*Omitted!* user PII suspected" for any search term value that looks like user PII)
results_count (number of results in the list after the filter is applied if applicable, e.g. "1", undefined if n/a like for Executive Dashboard work sample)
total_options (number of possible results in total when filters are not applied if applicable, e.g. "107", undefined if n/a like for Executive Dashboard work sample)
secondary_filter_applied (name and selection of enabled filter option if there's another filter applied in addition to the current filter selection, e.g. "Level: Expert", "Hostname: docs.larkspurlabs.com", undefined if n/a)
search_filter_applied (search term of enabled search filter if one is applied in addition to the current filter selection, e.g. "platform", undefined if n/a)
